Dataset: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10144972. Citation: Venugopal, V. & Olivetti, E. MatKG: An autonomously generated knowledge graph in Material Science. Scientific Data 11, 217 (2024), https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-024-03039-z. Changes: PRISM re-expressed the seven MatKG named-entity categories as OWL classes under a PRISM-minted namespace and loads the SUBRELOBJ co-occurrence rows as evidence-classed facts; entity names are percent-decoded but otherwise kept verbatim, including upstream NER dirt.

derivation.namespace_note: Class IRIs are PRISM-minted under https://mirdyne.com/ontology/matkg#. Upstream MatKG identifies entities and their types only under the placeholder namespace http://example.com/, and entity_uri_mapping.pickle (144,484 names) resolves every entity name to that same placeholder namespace, so no upstream canonical identity exists to reuse and http://example.com/ must not be propagated as identity. The original placeholder URI of each loaded entity is preserved additively in the entity's props_json as matkg_uri.
derivation.reification: Each SUBRELOBJ sro_row node carries exactly one hasSubject, hasRelationship, hasObject, and hasCount statement (measured: 5,396,084 rows, 21,584,336 statements, zero missing or duplicate fields). The loader joins the four statements per row; the entity class is the URI path segment of hasSubject/hasObject.
derivation.relationship_note: hasRelationship values are type-pair-shaped strings (e.g. CHM-PRO) that disagree with the subject/object URI type segments in the majority of rows measured (27,218 of 32,331 fully-joined rows in a 6M-line window), because the same name pair is tallied under multiple per-mention NER type contexts while entity URIs carry one canonical type per name. The value is therefore not trusted as a class or relation source; every loaded fact uses the single declared relationship cooccursWith, and the four-way join still requires the statement's presence.
derivation.semantics: The seven MatKG NER categories re-expressed as flat OWL classes (no subclass axioms are claimed upstream or asserted here), plus one object property for the statistical co-occurrence relationship. No OWL axioms beyond declarations and labels are asserted.
derivation.tool: hand-materialised from the MatKG 1.4 distribution and its Scientific Data paper

matched.rationale: MatKG CHM entities are chemicals/compounds/materials named in text; EMMO 1.0.3 declares Chemical in the vendored subset. closeMatch, not exactMatch, because MatKG members are NER strings, not curated chemical individuals.
MatKG PRO entities are material properties named in text; EMMO 1.0.3 declares Property in the vendored subset. closeMatch for the same NER-string reason.

emmo_alignment.scope: Alignment was asserted only against classes verifiably present in PRISM's vendored EMMO 1.0.3 subset (assets/ontology/emmo-1.0.3.materialised.ttl). An invented alignment is worse than an absent one.

unmatched.rationale: The nearest vendored EMMO class, Process, is strictly broader than a synthesis method (and MatKG SMT members include heavy NER noise); asserting closeMatch would overclaim. EMMO's Manufacturing branch is a candidate for future alignment but is not in the vendored subset to verify.
No application/use-context class exists in the vendored EMMO subset.
EMMO PhaseOfMatter denotes states of matter, while SPL members are symmetry/structure labels (and heavily noisy); the correspondence is not genuine enough for closeMatch.
No measurement/characterisation-method class exists in the vendored EMMO subset; EMMO's characterisation vocabulary lives in the separate CHAMEO module, which PRISM does not vendor.
MatKG DSC is a catch-all sample-descriptor category with no EMMO counterpart.

measured.note: Measured 2026-08-09 over the full pinned SUBRELOBJ.nt.tar.gz by streaming decompression; nothing extracted to disk.

paper: Venugopal, V. & Olivetti, E. MatKG: An autonomously generated knowledge graph in Material Science. Scientific Data 11, 217 (2024).

relation_mappings.rationale: The only relationship the SUBRELOBJ distribution actually carries is statistical co-occurrence; hasRelationship type-pair strings are not trusted (see derivation.relationship_note).
